use: Primary MIT course-author treatment of discrete capital accumulation, golden-rule consumption, monotone transition stability and labor-augmenting balanced growth; source conventions distinguished from the chapter's exact discrete growth law.
verification: Retrieved actual 87-slide official MIT PDF and inspected the model/accumulation and steady-state discussion in slides 1–27, golden-rule equations in slides 32–33, discrete transition definitions and full monotonicity proof in slides 37–44, labor-augmenting terminology in slide 64 and continuous-time balanced-growth discussion in slides 76–82. The chapter's golden-rule link gives the enclosing slides 28–33, with equations directly checked on 32–33. Continuous-time formulas are not represented as exact discrete laws. No graduate Uzawa theorem proof or complete empirical audit claimed; original cases/proofs, no copied figures or problems.
